headline: Labcorp to pay $2.3 million over medical-debt data breach
dek: A Connecticut-led coalition says Labcorp must pay the states and tighten vendor oversight after a 2019 breach at a debt collector potentially exposed information tied to 10.2 million patients.
body: Laboratory Corporation of America, known as Labcorp, will pay $2.287 million to 44 states and adopt new data-security requirements under a settlement announced Thursday by Connecticut Attorney General William Tong.

The case centers on a 2019 breach at American Medical Collection Agency, a Labcorp debt-collection vendor. State attorneys general say the intrusion potentially exposed personal information belonging to more than 27.5 million people nationwide, including 10.2 million Labcorp patients. Connecticut identified 43,666 affected patients; New York reported about 420,000.

The settlement assigns Connecticut $81,296 and requires Labcorp to strengthen its oversight of vendors that handle patient information. The changes include a dedicated vendor-risk team, contract cybersecurity requirements, inventories of debt collectors, security assessments and a third-party review of the company's information-security program.

The states' announcement distinguishes the Labcorp payment from an earlier settlement with AMCA that included a suspended $21 million payment after the collector's bankruptcy. Labcorp has also agreed to a separate $35 million class-action settlement that remains in litigation, according to the Connecticut attorney general's office.

The agreement does not mean every person whose information was potentially exposed suffered identity theft or financial loss. It does underscore the continuing responsibility of health-care companies to monitor contractors that receive sensitive medical and financial data, even when the breach occurs inside a vendor's systems.
